read: Read a text file or an image. Text is returned with line numbers, `offset` and `limit` bound the returned range, and a successful text read records the file revision required to edit or overwrite its current contents. PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP images are returned for visual inspection, downscaled to at most 2000 pixels on the longest side. To inspect a PDF or Office file visually, render the needed pages to PNG at a legible resolution and read only those, since each image adds substantial context. Office and PDF files are not text; read their contents through their format skills.
read_without_images: Read a text file with line numbers. `offset` and `limit` bound the returned range. A successful text read records the file revision required to edit or overwrite its current contents. Office and PDF files are not text; read them through their format skills.
edit: Make a text replacement in an existing file. Requires a prior read of the file's current contents; the call is rejected if the file changed since that read. `old_string` must match the current content, apart from line endings and leading or trailing whitespace; `new_string` is written exactly. `replace_all` changes every match instead of requiring a unique one. For changes in separate places, make separate edits: a replacement that spans unchanged text must retype it exactly, and any slip alters content outside the change.
write: Write the complete contents of a text file, creating parent directories when needed. This creates a new file or overwrites an existing one. Overwriting requires a prior read of the current contents and is rejected if the file changed since that read. The tool accepts text files only. Rewriting an existing file retypes all of it; for a local change, `edit` leaves the rest untouched.
grep: Search text files with a ripgrep-compatible regular expression. Results are bounded and include paths and line numbers. `include` optionally restricts filenames with a glob pattern. Directory searches exclude hidden and ignored files; an explicit file path searches that file. Patterns match within a single line, so a phrase wrapped across lines will not match. Office documents and PDFs store their text compressed or encoded, so their contents are not searched; search their extracted text instead. No match is not evidence that a document lacks the information.
glob: Find files by glob pattern beneath a directory. Results are bounded, sorted paths; hidden and ignored files are excluded.
bash: Run a Bash command in the configured execution environment. Each call starts a fresh shell process, and shell state does not carry between calls. Foreground commands run until they finish or reach their deadline (`timeout`, in milliseconds; 120,000 by default); raise it for long conversions or recalculations. With `run_in_background=true`, the call returns a managed task immediately, which suits servers, watchers, and long jobs you will inspect later; `task_list`, `task_output`, and `task_stop` list, inspect, and stop managed tasks. Retrieving saved output does not require running the command again.
task_output: Inspect a background Bash task. By default, wait up to the supplied timeout for the task to finish; set `block=false` to return its current state immediately. This wait does not change the task's process deadline. A still-running result or an elapsed wait does not mean the task finished or stopped.
